name: Go On
tagline: Most of the fights you've stopped never happened.
epigraph: This drink can sit on its ice while someone finishes talking. Someone once timed it.
language_row: Wren's 4-gram runs (the lint's own `ngrams()`) against every pour: clean after the fixes ("the way he told it" was *Standing By*'s, "what you give people" *The Other Berry*'s, "That's worth more than" *Any Day*'s, one *For Good* echo, two echoes of "peel squeezed over the top"). Every "he" is Jimmie or Arnold, never the guest (lint warnings accepted by Wren). whoYouAre runs 166 words, accepted by Wren: both paragraphs carry a must-have. No boxing, no jokes beat (*Worth the Trip*), no "fooled them" (*No Accident*). ✓

names_note: **Go On**, the room's pick (all three): the guest's own words to the person talking, and the drink's gesture (the wait). Runner-up for Robin: *To Each Other* (Wren's first pick, the toast Jimmie got out of two people about to fight; conceded in r4: it names his outcome, not the person). Also considered: *When You're Ready*, *Hear Them Out*, *On the Ice*, *Forget to Be Angry*. Wren's worry, carried to Robin: cold, "Go On" could sound like "go on, have another"; the tagline steers it back to people.
open_items: **Memoir read in OCR highlights only:** *This Must Be the Place* is lending-only on archive.org; every Charters line is from full-text search highlights, told through a ghost-writer (Morrill Cody). A full read could confirm the joins in F5.

**Jimmie's Dingo cocktail:** the cognac fraction is OCR-garbled, so the room claims no proportions, only that it had cognac and "Mandarin" in it (his bottle unnamed). Ours is a stirred cognac Manhattan, a riff, never "his recipe".
**Unsourced numbers (Tomás):** the mandarin liqueur's 38% and 25 g/100 ml are estimates; every sweep stop (18–35 g, 30–40%, cognac 40–45%, drier vermouth) stays in range.
**Arnold's test transferred:** *Liquid Intelligence* tested a rye Manhattan (15 s stir, 90 s on the ice); carrying it to a cognac Manhattan is Tomás's craft call, written as one.

**Family claims:** the plan reserved cognac (as a style) for the Revolutionary, and the Magnetic Leader holds the plain rye Manhattan (Ciro's, also Paris). Different cocktails; the two readings must never share an opening. The plan's Bilgray lead was overturned by Wren (r1); the Plunkett/Masterson lead was struck on the 1906 press (Hester r2).
**Name:** *Go On* vs *To Each Other*, for Robin's eye (see Names considered).
